chapters.title: Designing for resilience and region pairs

takeaways: Availability zones are physically separate groups of datacenters inside a region, but Azure does not spread your resources across them automatically.
Availability sets protect VMs against rack and maintenance failures within one datacenter, while zones and zone-redundant services protect against losing a whole building.
SLAs are refund policies, region pairs are not automatic disaster recovery, and real uptime comes from deliberate design, backups and tested failover.
hook: Most people assume an app in the cloud keeps running no matter what, but a single zone failure can still take it offline. This beginner-friendly episode explains Azure regions, availability zones, availability sets and region pairs for anyone deploying workloads to Azure. You will learn what the SLA numbers really mean and how to design uptime as a deliberate choice.
